NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notices to Congress, Cockroach Janta Party, AAP and AISA after taking note of an amended plea by traders' bodies alleging that their businesses were affected by protests held in Delhi.During the hearing, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that competing fundamental rights - the right to protest and the right to conduct business - must be balanced.Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, representing the traders' bodies, submitted that protests at Jantar Mantar disrupted businesses in Central Delhi, Live Law reported.He also raised objections to the designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue."I am also saying that Ramlila Ground is in the heart of the city. Protests should not be allowed there when wholesale markets are situated all around Ramlila Ground," Rohatgi said.The bench said that the traders' petition would be heard along with other petitions questioning the restrictions imposed by the authorities in the wake of protests in the national capital.The petitions are tentatively listed for hearing on November 27.
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues notices to Congress, Cockroach Janta Party, AAP and AISA. Court takes note of an amended plea by traders' bodies alleging that their businesses were affected by protests held in Delhi. Chief Justice Surya Kant said competing fundamental rights - the right to protest and to conduct business - must be balanced.

Article Title: 'Youth must know what UP was like 10 years ago': CM Yogi renews 'batenge toh katenge' pitch
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended slogans such as “Batenge toh katenge” and “Ek hain toh safe hain”, saying they were intended to remind people of the state's past law-and-order problems and encourage vigilance rather than polarise voters.Speaking at the News18 Rising Bharat Summit: North Edition, Adityanath said the younger generation needed to understand the conditions in Uttar Pradesh a decade ago to appreciate the changes made since then.“The question is not of polarisation; it is of being alert and cautious,” he said, according to news agency ANI.The chief minister said young people, particularly those aged between 15 and 25-27, should learn about the circumstances their parents had experienced. He alleged that Uttar Pradesh had faced an identity crisis, riots, lawlessness, insecurity among women and extortion during the previous Samajwadi Party (SP) government.“Today's youth, particularly those aged between 15 and 25-27 years, need to know what Uttar Pradesh was like 10 years ago. They need to understand the circumstances their parents went through,” he said.Explaining the slogan “Batenge toh katenge”, Adityanath referred to incidents during the SP government's tenure, including the Jawahar Bagh violence in Mathura, the Muzaffarnagar riots and communal clashes in Kosi Kalan, Aligarh and Bareilly.He alleged that riots were frequent under the SP government, while claiming that Uttar Pradesh was now “riot-free and curfew-free” under the BJP administration.Referring to the 2016 Jawahar Bagh violence, the chief minister alleged that a person associated with the SP had occupied hundreds of acres of land in the park.Two police personnel, then Superintendent of Police Mukul Dwivedi and Station House Officer Santosh Yadav, were killed during the operation to clear the encroachment. Adityanath said 23 people died in the incident.He also alleged that statues of social reformers and national leaders, including BR Ambedkar, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Mahatma Gandhi, had been targeted during previous governments.Adityanath said the present could be understood only by looking at the past and urged young people to take responsibility for sustaining the changes made in the state.“The present is safe only when we look at the past. The future will be dignified only when the present improves,” he said.“The present has improved because we have rectified the mistakes made by the previous government in the past,” he added.Asked whether law and order and Hindutva would be the two major issues in the coming Assembly elections, Adityanath said the focus would be on “security and nationalism”, along with “cultural nationalism”.“We will ensure development for everyone and make efforts to take everyone along, but there will be no appeasement of anyone,” he said.He maintained that the government's welfare approach was based on ensuring that all eligible beneficiaries received assistance without discrimination.Citing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis on the “saturation” of welfare schemes, Adityanath said beneficiary lists were prepared using existing data rather than by BJP workers.“There is no pick and choose now,” he said, adding that separate policies had also been formulated to include needy people left out of existing lists.The chief minister also defended the BJP's political messaging around Mathura, including the slogan “Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De” and references to Ayodhya and Mathura. He said religious and cultural centres “are matters of faith for us and not merely election agendas”.Adityanath said his government had worked towards the revival and development of more than 4,500 ancient temples and religious sites across Uttar Pradesh.He cited the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, saying it had improved access to the shrine and enabled around 50,000 devotees to visit at a time. He also referred to the development of Ayodhya, including the international airport named after Lord Ram, and projects in Mathura-Vrindavan, Prayagraj and other pilgrimage centres.He said a four-lane road and a corridor had been developed at Govardhan in connection with the religious site associated with Sant Ravidas, along with the installation of his statue.The chief minister alleged that previous Congress and SP governments had obstructed the development of religious centres because of their appeasement policies.He also claimed that funds earlier spent on encroachments and boundary walls around graveyards were now being used for pilgrimage centre development.Opposition parties have criticised the “Batenge toh katenge” slogan, arguing that it carries communal overtones. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had compared it to the British policy of divide and rule.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath defends slogans such as “Batenge toh katenge” and “Ek hain toh safe hain” He says they are intended to remind people of the state's past law- and-order problems and encourage vigilance rather than polarise voters. He alleged that Uttar Pradesh had faced an identity crisis, riots, lawlessness, insecurity among women and extortion during the previous Samajwadi Party (SP) government.

NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat, the only surviving local terrorist in the Valley, was trapped in an ongoing encounter in Kulgam district. Despite being cornered, the most wanted terrorist refused to surrender despite an offer from security forces, news agency PTI reported, quoting officials on Wednesday.The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced the morning prayers.Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was urged to surrender. Videos of security forces appealing to him to lay down his arms surfaced on social media.Also Read| 'Some dishes best served cold': Top LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam encounter However, LeT commander Bhat refused to surrender.Security forces are exercising maximum restraint in the ongoing encounter with Lashkar commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, as the trapped terrorist is firing from inside a mosque located within the cordoned-off area, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Kulgam said.The encounter was launched following credible intelligence inputs from Jammu and Kashmir Police and was carried out with proper planning and coordination among security forces, the SSP said.Security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including speaking to him over a video call for an extended period. The SSP said they appealed to him to lay down his arms, reminding him that he was young and could still surrender, but he refused."He chose to take shelter inside a mosque. We made repeated announcements, urging him to surrender, but he did not relent. At around 3.45, he opened fire on security forces, triggering a gunfight," the SSP Anayat Ali Choudhary said.He stressed that security forces were exercising utmost restraint as the mosque was located in the middle of the cordoned-off area and the terrorist was firing from inside the religious structure."I would like to emphasise that we are setting an example by exercising maximum restraint, particularly because the mosque is located in the middle of the cordoned-off area. The terrorist is firing from inside the mosque. I want to assure you that we have maintained the utmost restraint and are strictly following the standard operating procedures (SOPs). We will neutralise the terrorist, but we will take the time necessary to do so. Time is on our side," he said.The SSP added that security forces were trying to ensure minimal damage to the mosque while working to neutralise the terrorist as soon as possible."For now, we are having maximum restraint. We will ensure that the mosque is minimally damaged. We will try to eliminate the terrorist as soon as possible," he said.The encounter comes two days after Umar Nisar Dar, one of the terrorists involved in the November 11 attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam, was killed in a gunfight near Laru bypass on Monday. Bhat had escaped from the encounter site.Both Bhat and Dar are suspected of carrying out the attack on the CRPF post, which left three paramilitary personnel injured.Earlier, Kashmir Zone Police announced the encounter on X, saying, "Encounter started with terrorists and joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam."After Dar was killed on Monday, security forces continued extensive searches across the area to track down Bhat. Contact with him was re-established during searches early Wednesday, triggering a fresh exchange of gunfire.Officials said Dar had allegedly sheltered Bhat and provided logistical support to him for nearly six months. The duo is also suspected of conducting reconnaissance before carrying out the attack on the CRPF post last week.Dar, a former breadmaker who had been reported missing by his family, was killed in the encounter on Monday, a week after joining The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based LeT.
Article Summary: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat was trapped in an ongoing encounter in Kulgam district. Despite being cornered, the most wanted terrorist refused to surrender despite an offer from security forces. The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced the morning prayers.

Article Title: 'Sitting on disaster': Rahul Gandhi flags India's economic 'crisis' during US visit; BJP hits back

BJP hits back

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said India was heading towards an economic crisis, citing massive unemployment and deep-rooted concerns over the country's education system. He made the remarks during an event at Columbia University in New York as part of his US visit.Rahul's comments drew a strong response from the ruling BJP, with the party calling him a "leader of anti-India propaganda.""The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system,"Lok Sabha leader of opposition said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The former Congress president was responding to a question from moderator about India's youth. He said a section of young people expressing frustration with the current state of affairs came from middle-class families and had received formal education, but were increasingly disillusioned with their prospects."We've been studying this, we've been looking into this, and the reason is very interesting, which is that the crux of it is they do not see a future for themselves," he said.Rahul said that there was a growing disconnect between young people and their parents over career opportunities, saying the younger generation was questioning the advice and experiences of the previous generation."So what they're actually saying to their parents, and we're hearing this from the parents, listen, You're not successful, you don't have a job, you can't tell us to do what you did because it doesn't work," he said.He said unemployment, limited future opportunities and concerns about the education system were pressing challenges that could not be brushed aside.BJP hit back at Rahul over his remarks in the US, accusing the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad.Leading the charge, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari took to X and called Rahul a "leader of anti-India propaganda"."Rahul Gandhi insults India at Columbia University! Rahul Gandhi calls India "Economic Disaster" & speaks against Indian Democracy!" Bhandari wrote.He further accused Rahul of harbouring "inherent hate for India's progress& Indian democracy", alleging that the Congress leader spoke ill of India whenever he travelled abroad.Drawing a comparison with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Bhandari said the PM upheld India's national interests and respected the spirit of the national flag during official foreign visits."Rahul Gandhi insults spirit of India's national flag by speaking against India democracy! Rahul Gandhi is a disaster as a responsible LOP!" he added.Rahul is on a two-day visit to the United States. He is scheduled to visit the University of Chicago on Tuesday, November 18.
Article Summary: BJP hit back at Rahul over his remarks in the US, accusing the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad. He said unemployment, limited future opportunities and concerns about the education system were pressing challenges that could not be brushed aside. Rahul is on a two-day visit to the United States.

Article Title: 'Goldy Dhillon a petty thief': Lawrence gang on gangster who threatened Amitabh Bachchan

NEW DELHI: Gangster Goldy Dhillon had a narrow escape in Germany during an attack by the Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Canada handler, Manna Brampton, and his Madrid counterpart, Mandeep Spain, in Jan this year, the duo said in a statement on social media Tuesday.A day after Dhillon's post threatening actor Amitabh Bachchan, the duo hit out at Dhillon for killing an LGBTQ+ influencer, Mad Sandhu, in Amritsar and called him "publicity hungry" for targeting Bachchan.Claiming Dhillon used to wash utensils at a restaurant in Germany for a living, they said he lacked the wherewithal to target Bachchan or even his domestic staff.Calling Dhillon's claims of seeking revenge for the 1984 anti-Sikh riots a desperate bid for attention, Brampton and Spain said he was no-thing more than a petty thief and a "chitta" (heroin) peddler from Punjab with FIRs against him for drug-dealing and stealing cable wires.On the attack, the gang said despite constantly boasting about weapons, Dhillon had nothing but a knife to defend himself. He managed to escape and subsequently fled the country, they claimed.Furthermore, the former associates said they were the ones who had helped Dhillon gain a footing in the underworld by carrying out for free three murders and 20-25 firings in Canada to establish his name.In a damning blow to his credibility in the underworld, Brampton and Spain also labelled Dhillon a police informer.They claimed after using henchmen to commit crimes, Dhillon would tip off cops to get his operatives arrested, while posting about the incidents online to take credit. Challenging Dhillon to a face-off in any country, the duo warned others against associating with him.The post, sources said, prima facie confirmed speculation that Dhillon had parted ways with the Lawrence gang. In his post against Bachchan Monday, Dhillon did not mention Lawrence Bishnoi, even as he named a number of operatives, including Rocky Portugal and Suman Germany.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi gang's Canada handler, Manna Brampton, and his Madrid counterpart, Mandeep Spain, hit out at Dhillon for killing an LGBTQ+ influencer, Mad Sandhu, in Amritsar. They called him "publicity hungry" for targeting Amitabh Bachchan. They said he lacked the wherewithal to target Bachchan or his domestic staff.

Article Title: In a first, Xi receives Trump in Shenzhen ahead of historic trilateral summit with Putin
Article Text:
Trump lands in China for historic trilateral summit with Xi, Putin

US president Donald Trump arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where he was received by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the airport.He is also scheduled to hold a trilateral meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.Trump has said he intends to discuss limiting nuclear weapons and ending the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 following Russia's invasion. However, his aides had earlier told reporters that the Ukraine conflict would not feature in the trilateral meeting.The US president said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opportunity to resolve the conflict, expressing optimism about the prospects of an agreement.“I think it’s very close to getting it done,” Trump said. “We’re going to have a good meeting on that.”Trump also raised the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, although neither engagement has been confirmed.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was “serious” about meeting Kim to address tensions with North Korea. However, he indicated that no meeting between the two leaders had been scheduled for Thursday.“I’m not telling you that there will be a meeting tomorrow,” Rubio said. “I’m just saying that" the president "is willing to meet and discuss, as he did during his first term.”Trump's visit to China follows his participation in the Asean summit and the Quad leaders' meeting in Manila. Shortly before leaving the Philippines, he announced a new trade agreement with the country in a post on Truth Social."I am now heading to China, from the Philippines, where we had a wonderful meeting on Trade, National Security, and other subjects. I am pleased to announce that we made a new and completely different Trade Deal with the Philippines, one that will be a true landmark and, in particular, a Deal that will be great for our Farmers and those in the business of “Energy.” President Marcos is a powerful leader, and a man of high integrity and substance. It was an Honor to be with him, and his beautiful wife and son. See you in China."Earlier on Wednesday, Putin held bilateral talks with Xi in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC forum, with both leaders emphasising the importance of strengthening Russia-China ties and advancing a multipolar world order.Putin said the two countries must work towards shaping a fairer multipolar world, while describing their foreign policy relationship as stable and positive."Russia and China work to shape a fairer multipolar world order amid a challenging geopolitical situation. The Russian-Chinese foreign policy relationship remains stable and on a positive footing," Putin said.Xi echoed the Russian leader's remarks, calling on both countries to take the lead in advancing multipolarisation and democratisation in international relations amid global uncertainty."We must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers lead and advance the multipolarisation of the world and the democratisation of international relations," Xi said.He also called for deeper cooperation across various sectors, saying the partnership had contributed to stability in an increasingly turbulent international environment."Our relationship has brought greater stability and certainity to a turbulent world."Xi further described Russia-China relations as a model of equality, mutual respect and mutually beneficial cooperation.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday to attend the Asia- Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. He is also scheduled to hold a trilateral meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump has said he intends to discuss limiting nuclear weapons and ending the war in Ukraine.

Article Title: Watch: PM Modi picks up Tricolour from floor at Quad photo op; Trump reacts
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with US President Donald Trump during the Quad Leaders Meeting, in Manila

PM Modi highlights Quad's role in Indo-Pacific

Trump praises PM Modi, announces Quad initiatives

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi picked up a small Indian flag being used as a spot marker during a group photograph of Quad leaders in Manila on Tuesday, prompting a reaction from US president Donald Trump The moment unfolded as PM Modi was taking his place alongside Trump, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese and Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi for the media ahead of their meeting on the sidelines of the Asean summit in the Philippine capital.As PM Modi picked up the flag marker, he said he could not leave the national flag on the floor.“I cannot put (leave the flag) on the floor,” he said.Trump responded: “Save it.”The gesture recalled a similar moment during the 2023 BRICS summit in Johannesburg, when Modi picked up an Indian flag marker from the stage.The photograph preceded the Quad leaders' meeting, during which PM Modi described the grouping as a “constructive and trusted partnership” and called for concrete goals to guide its next phase of cooperation across the Indo-Pacific.Addressing the other three leaders, PM Modi pointed to Manila's long association with the grouping. Officials from the four countries first met in the city in 2007, while their dialogue was revived there in 2017.He said the foreign ministers of the four countries had met five times since January last year, calling this evidence of their “political will and shared commitment” to the partnership.“For India, the Quad is a constructive and trusted partnership.From maritime security to trusted supply chains, new technologies to disaster response, it has been our endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions,” he said.PM Modi expressed confidence that the meeting would help establish concrete goals for the next phase of cooperation and thanked the other leaders for their continued support.Trump also praised PM Modi during the meeting, calling him a friend and a leader respected around the world.“He is a tough man. He is my friend. He is a great leader and respected all over the world,” Trump said, adding that relations between the US and India were “outstanding” and that the two countries were coordinating closely.Trump also outlined four initiatives emerging from the meeting: a Quad Business Leaders' Forum, a Super Intelligence Accelerator, a Maritime Intelligence Sharing Corporation and cooperation on cybersecurity intelligence-sharing.The Quad, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, has broadened its agenda beyond traditional security concerns to include resilient supply chains, critical minerals, emerging technologies, infrastructure and disaster response.
Article Summary: PM Modi picks up small Indian flag being used as a spot marker during a group photograph of Quad leaders in Manila. US president Donald Trump responds: "Save it" The gesture recalled a similar moment during the 2023 BRICS summit in Johannesburg, when Modi picked up an Indian flag marker from the stage.

SRINAGAR: Security forces intensified searches in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district Tuesday to track wounded TRF terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, who escaped after Monday’s gunfight that killed his associate and new recruit Umar Nisar Dar in Larnoo.Police sources said Dar had recently gone missing, prompting his family to lodge a report at Kulgam police station. He had allegedly assisted Bhat for months before joining TRF, a side-shoot of Lashkar-e-Taiba, after the attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam’s Mir Bazar on Nov 11 that left three personnel wounded. Dar and Bhat allegedly conducted reconnaissance at several locations, including Mir Bazar, on Nov 10.Bhat from Khrewan Chader village in Kulgam carries a Rs 15 lakh reward announced in Aug. He is accused of killing a J&K police head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July last year.The prolonged search and restrictions across villages drew criticism from political parties. CPM MLA MY Tarigami, PDP politician Iltija Mufti and NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar accused security forces of subjecting civilians, including women, children and elderly people, to indiscriminate frisking and harassment. They said action against those responsible for the attack should not cause hardship to innocent residents.

Article Title: 'Tough man, great leader': Trump heaps praise on PM Modi at crucial Quad meeting
Article Text:

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with the leaders of the Quad grouping in Manila, describing him as a "tough man", a "great leader" and his friend, who is "respected all over the world"."He is a tough man," Trump said on PM Modi "He is my friend. He is a great leader and respected all over the world.""We have outstanding relationships, coordinating closely," Trump said while addressing the Quad leaders, adding that the grouping represented "some of the most successful partnerships in the world".Trump arrived in the Philippine capital on Tuesday for the 49th Asean Summit , where he is scheduled to meet regional leaders and discuss trade and security cooperation. Manila is the first stop on his three-day Asian tour, which will also take him to China for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.Trump has also indicated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during the visit.Trump's schedule in Manila includes the Quad meeting, a trade deal with Thailand and a special summit with Asean leaders, followed by a gala dinner where he is the guest of honour.The trip marks Trump's first overseas visit since his Republican Party suffered significant losses in the midterm elections. His visit comes amid domestic challenges, including a major disruption to the US aviation industry and controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former chief executive Jensen Huang, who was linked to a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent. Beijing has denied involvement.The Asean discussions are expected to focus on strengthening trade and security ties, as well as regional challenges, including the ongoing conflict in Myanmar and tensions in the South China Sea. The region has seen growing confrontations between Chinese and Philippine maritime forces over disputed waters, which are a key global trade route.The Quad, comprising the US, India, Japan and Australia, aims to counter China's growing influence in the Indo-Pacific. The Manila meeting is the grouping's first leaders' engagement since Trump returned to the White House last year.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a meeting with the leaders of the Quad grouping in Manila. Trump arrived in the Philippine capital on Tuesday for the 49th Asean Summit. Manila is the first stop on his three-day Asian tour, which will also take him to China.

Article Title: NIA files case to probe Rajouri network facilitating LeT, JeM
Article Text:
The accused said they acted as guides and facilitated the movement of Pakistani terrorists towards Kashmir Valley (representative image)

JAMMU: NIA has registered a case to probe a network of over-ground workers (OGW) facilitating the activities of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba ( LeT ) and Jaish-e-Mohammed ( JeM ) terrorist outfits in Jammu & Kashmir.“The NIA case stems from an FIR registered by J&K police into a terror ecosystem that was busted in Rajouri’s Pir Panjal region in Sept,” an NIA spokesperson said Tuesday.Police arrested Zakir Hussain, Mohammed Azam, and Mohd Mushtaq on Sept 14. During interrogation, the accused said they acted as guides and facilitated the movement of Pakistani terrorists towards Kashmir Valley, besides providing support for terror attacks.An IED was recovered on the disclosure of one of the arrested accused. The device was handed over to an OGW by terrorists for safe custody and its use in a targeted attack, police said.
Article Summary: Police arrested Zakir Hussain, Mohammed Azam, and Mohd Mushtaq on Sept 14. During interrogation, the accused said they acted as guides and facilitated the movement of Pakistani terrorists towards Kashmir Valley. An IED was recovered on the disclosure of one of the arrested accused.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Bihar LoP Tejashwi Yadav on Tuesday criticised the naming of the Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge as 'Nitish Setu', claiming that then CM Nitish Kumar had earlier agreed to name it after freedom fighter Akshayvat Rai.Speaking on the controversy in Patna, Tejashwi said the foundation stone for the bridge was laid when the Mahagathbandhan government came to power in 2015-16. He said he had then requested Nitish Kumar to name the bridge after Rai, a freedom fighter and close associate of former Bihar chief minister Karpoori Thakur.“He was a freedom fighter and a very close associate of Karpoori Thakur; the bridge actually passes right by his home. At that time, Nitish ji agreed,” Tejashwi said.The RJD leader alleged that Nitish Kumar was currently not in a proper state of mind and claimed that the bridge would have been named after Akshayvat Rai had the chief minister been mentally fit.“Had he been in a sound state of mind, the bridge would have been named after Akshayvat Rai, but currently, he is not in a proper state of mind,” Tejashwi said.He also recalled that he had reviewed the project after becoming deputy chief minister again in 2022 to ensure its timely progress.“At that time, we had taken loans and invested several thousand crore rupees from our own resources. The Bihar government funded it through its own resources and by taking on debt,” he said.The naming of the bridge after Nitish Kumar has triggered a political debate in Bihar. Nitish Kumar inaugurated the first phase of the bridge on June 23, 2025, when he was chief minister. The section connects Kachchi Dargah in Patna with Raghopur diara island in Vaishali district.BJP national president Nitin Nabin said that Kumar had helped Bihar move beyond “jungle raj” towards good governance.
Article Summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav criticised the naming of the Kacchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge as 'Nitish Setu' He claimed that then CM Nitish Kumar had earlier agreed to name it after freedom fighter Akshayvat Rai.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday condemned the missile attack on a Panama flagged tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz.In a statement, the ministry said 21 of the 24 Indian nationals had been safely evacuated, while two crew members were injured and one remained missing. The ministry added that the Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations."We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT TARA GAS in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 2026. Of the 24 Indian nationals on board, 21 have been safely evacuated ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian crew members have been admitted to hospital, while one Indian national remains missing," the ministry said."Our Embassy in Oman is closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations in coordination with the Omani authorities. We appreciate the timely assistance and support extended by the Government of Oman in the rescue efforts," it added.MEA also reiterated that the continuing attacks on shipping in the region were "worrisome" and posed a serious threat to the safety of civilian seafarers."The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," the ministry said.Earlier, in a social media post on X, Sonowal said, "All 24 Indian nationals, along with the entire 25-member crew, are completely safe with no injuries."We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers," he said.Hours later, Sonowal, in a post on X, further said that in a distressing development, the Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS was subjected to a subsequent attack, forcing the entire crew to abandon the vessel."While 24 crew members have been safely accounted for, one Indian seafarer remains missing," he said."We are urgently coordinating with the ship management company and regional rescue authorities to locate our missing seafarer and ensure the immediate safety, welfare and logistical support of the rescued crew members," the minister added.
Article Summary: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday condemned the missile attack on a Panama flagged tanker carrying 24 Indian seafarers. 21 of the 24 Indian nationals had been safely evacuated, while two crew members were injured and one remained missing. The Indian Embassy in Oman was closely monitoring the ongoing search and rescue operations.

The CJI asked the petitioner’s counsel to make detailed submissions when the matter comes up before the appropriate bench on Friday.Advocate Rizwan Ahmed sought urgent intervention, alleging that Filibeck, the Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had interfered in India’s domestic political affairs by criticising the government and expressing support for the Opposition at the summit.Seeking an early hearing, Ahmed told the bench that the event had been organised in Telangana under the aegis of the state government and certain foundations, including the Samruddha Bharat Foundation. Article Title: US midterms: Alaska turns blue as Peltola defeats Sullivan, seals 56-44 Democratic Senate majority
Article Text:
Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola

Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's US Senate race, flipping the ninth Republican-held seat to her party and giving Democrats a 56-44 majority in the chamber when the new Congress begins in January.The victory marks the Democrats' biggest midterm Senate gain in nearly 70 years. The party last gained nine or more seats in a midterm election in 1958, when it captured 15 seats during Republican President Dwight Eisenhower's second term, according to historical US election data cited by AP.Peltola secured 50 per cent of first-preference votes against Sullivan's 46 per cent, clearing the threshold required to win outright under Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, projections by US media showed.Her victory came despite Alaska voting for US president Donald Trump by 13 percentage points in 2024. Voter concerns over the rising cost of living, along with the state's independent political streak, helped make the contest competitive.In a post on X after media projected her victory, Peltola said, "As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.""Thank you, Alaska. Let’s get to work," she added.The campaign's final stretch was overshadowed by allegations that Democrats had helped recruit an independent candidate, Dan J. Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher, to split votes and confuse supporters of the Republican incumbent. Republican Gerry Heikes was also on the general-election ballot.Republicans sought to remove Sullivan Jr., arguing that he was not a "good faith" candidate. The Alaska Supreme Court rejected the challenge.The New York Times reported shortly before Election Day that Peltola's campaign had helped recruit Sullivan Jr. Her campaign denied involvement. Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered a state investigation, saying it was examining anything that could "resemble perjury".The Justice Department also opened a criminal investigation. US attorney general Todd Blanche described the reported recruitment effort as "fraud". Reuters previously reported that the department had issued more than 140 subpoenas, letters and notices in the probe, though these actions do not establish wrongdoing.Peltola's victory was the final Senate race to be called, completing nine Republican-held seat flips. Democrats had already secured their eighth pickup with Scott Colom's victory in Mississippi.The party also reclaimed the House of Representatives, gaining 42 seats as of Tuesday.
Article Summary: Mary Peltola defeated Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. Victory marks the Democrats' biggest midterm Senate gain in nearly 70 years. Democrats had already secured their eighth pickup with Scott Colom's victory in Mississippi. The party also reclaimed the House of Representatives, gaining 42 seats as of Tuesday.

MUMBAI: After nine years, four judges, a divorce, claims that the victim was seen alive, bail for the three accused and an almost year-long delay caused by the pandemic, the prosecution has closed its evidence in the Supreme Court-expedited Sheena Bora murder trial after examining 150 witnesses. The prosecution communicated this to the special CBI court on Tuesday.On trial are former media executive Indrani Mukerjea and her former husbands Peter Mukerjea and Sanjeev Khanna Unless the accused choose to examine defence witnesses, the special CBI court will record their statements under Section 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, with questions framed based on the evidence placed during the trial. This will be followed by final arguments by both sides. The court will then reserve the judgment.CBI has alleged that Indrani, Peter, Khanna and driver Shyamvar Rai conspired to abduct and murder her daughter, Sheena Bora, from an earlier relationship. It said on April 24, 2012, Indrani, Khanna and Rai abducted Sheena in a car, sedated and strangled her, and later disposed of her body in a forest in Pen, Raigad.The alleged murder came to light in Aug 2015 during Rai’s interrogation by Khar police following his arrest in an illegal arms case.Indrani and Khanna were arrested. In Nov 2015, when police filed a chargesheet against Indrani, Khanna and Rai, Peter was also arrested and charged with murder and conspiracy. The case was handed over to CBI. Rai later turned approver and deposed as a prosecution witness.In Jan 2017, the court framed charges against the accused for murder, destruction of evidence, criminal conspiracy, kidnapping and giving false information about an offence. Indrani and Khanna were also charged with attempting to murder Mekhail; no such charge was framed against Peter. All pleaded not guilty.The key witnesses included Rai; Sheena’s father, Siddhartha Das; Indrani’s son, Mekhail Bora; her daughter with Khanna, Vidhie Mukerjea; Peter’s son from an earlier marriage, Rahul Mukerjea, who was engaged to Sheena; Indrani’s former assistant, Kajal Sharma; former housekeeper Pradeep Waghmare; and IPS officer Deven Bharti. The last witness was CBI investigating officer K K Singh.In Dec 2023, the CBI submitted a list of 23 witnesses it would not examine. Among the “unreliable witnesses” was former Mumbai police commissioner Rakesh Maria. During city police’s investigation, Maria was appointed director general, Home Guards.Among the motives alleged by CBI was Peter and Indrani’s opposition to Sheena’s relationship with Rahul. Despite their disapproval, Rahul and Sheena had got engaged and were planning to marry in 2012, the agency claimed.The trial began in Feb 2017 with the deposition of police officer Ganesh Dalvi. The defence objected on legal grounds when he began deposing about Rai’s alleged confession, arguing that criminal procedure and evidence law did not permit use of statements made to a police officer as a confession. The objection briefly halted proceedings.Rai, the prosecution’s star witness, took the stand in July 2017. His testimony, which largely matched his confession statement before a magistrate, detailed the alleged planning and execution of the murder in Indrani’s car and the disposal of Sheena’s body. The trial then proceeded steadily, with 67 witnesses examined by 2020.In Oct 2019, while in custody, Indrani and Peter ended their marriage by mutual consent. They had married in 2002. In March 2020, Peter was granted bail by Bombay HC, days before the Covid lockdown stalled the trial. Proceedings resumed in Feb 2021 with the cross-examination of the 67th witness, a handwriting expert, who had last deposed in March 2020.The trial faced another delay in late 2024 when the presiding judge was transferred. In March 2025, special CBI judge J P Darekar said the trial would resume on a day-to-day basis from March 10, following HC’s directions. Darekar is the fourth judge to preside over the case after H S Mahajan, J C Jagdale and S P Naik-Nimbalkar.A twist came in Dec 2021, when Indrani wrote to CBI claiming that a Byculla jail inmate had told her Sheena was alive and living in Kashmir. CBI dismissed the claim as a “figment of imagination”. Indrani later said she wanted to keep the plea on hold.In May 2022, SC granted Indrani bail. She later wrote a book, appeared in an OTT documentary on the case and acted in plays. In June 2022, Bombay HC granted Khanna bail.

On trial are former media executive Indrani Mukerjea and her former husbands. Unless the accused choose to examine defence witnesses, the special. CBI court will record their statements under Section 313 of Criminal Procedure Code.

Article Title: How Bengaluru man's meeting with pal turned fatal; gunned down in car

Imraz Pasha, a Bengaluru scrap dealer, was found shot dead in his car

Licensed pistol used in killing?

BENGALURU: A 45-year-old scrap dealer who was meeting a business associate on Monday afternoon was found shot dead in his hatchback car in east Bengaluru on Tuesday morning, with multiple bullet injuries to his head.Police identified the deceased as Imraz Pasha, a resident of Bannerghatta Road. He was found dead in the front seat of the car in Papanna Layout, Manchappanahalli village.Preliminary investigations said a passerby noticed the parked car with a dead man inside. Article Title: House of cards: 22 lives lost in 6 Delhi building collapses since September
Article Text:
Recent building collapses in Delhi have led to 22 fatalities and 27 injuries in a short span.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





NEW DELHI: In less than three months, a spate of building and structural collapses across Delhi has claimed 22 lives and left at least 27 people injured, bringing into sharp focus concerns over the safety of ageing and dilapidated structures, unauthorised construction and inadequate enforcement of building safety regulations in the city.These casualties were reported across six major building collapses since Sept. In the first incident, a building in Satya Niketan killed seven people and injured five others on Sept 6. In Oct, structural collapses claimed six lives and left eight people injured. The toll rose further in Nov, with nine people losing their lives and 14 sustaining injuries in building-collapse incidents reported up to Nov 17.Former Delhi Fire Service chief Atul Garg said building collapses are often caused by two major factors. The first is the lack of a proper structural assessment before construction, with buildings frequently being erected in haste without adequately examining the strength and stability of the structure.“Builders often fail to pay attention to critical aspects, such as whether lintels have been properly installed and whether the supporting materials have sufficiently dried and settled before further construction is undertaken,” he pointed out.The second factor, according to him, could be water seepage, which gradually weakens the structural integrity of a building. Garg said property owners often ignore signs of seepage and fail to undertake timely repairs or maintenance, allowing the damage to worsen over time and potentially leading to a structural failure or collapse.According to DFS data, till Oct 26, the department received 396 calls related to house collapses. The situation was no different in 2025, when more than 500 calls were received.Professor V K Paul, director, School of Planning and Architecture, said there were several reasons behind collapses. A key factor is the absence of proper architectural and structural design, with buildings often constructed without following established processes or involving competent engineers and contractors.Another reason, he said, is the modification of structures after construction, which can adversely affect their stability. He said old buildings do not collapse suddenly but usually show signs of structural distress gradually, which need to be identified and addressed in time.A third factor is the condition of the soil, he said. The presence of water beneath or around a building can weaken the ground and affect its foundation, potentially leading to subsidence. Construction activity without considering impact on neighbouring buildings can also compromise the stability of an existing structure.Paul stressed the need for a graded inspection system to assess buildings, identify those showing signs of structural distress and prioritise in a graded manner for timely repairs and necessary interventions.
Article Summary: In less than three months, a spate of building and structural collapses across Delhi has claimed 22 lives and left at least 27 people injured. These casualties were reported across six major building collapses since Sept. The toll rose further in Nov, with nine people losing their lives and 14 sustaining injuries in building-collapse incidents.

Article Title: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
Article Text:
US flight chaos enters third day, over 10,000 flights hit

One router, a chain of problems: What went wrong

FAA still has no clear answer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday.He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.The trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.The technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions."We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.
Article Summary: More than 10,000 flights cancelled or delayed for third day in a row. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said things could return to normal by Monday. The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration is yet to identify the exact cause.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: 'Oh wow, fantastic': Trump reacts as Philippine prez sends fried chicken as late-night 'taste of Manila'
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump and Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ​​

Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arranged a late-night delivery of fried chicken from homegrown fast-food chain Jollibee for US president Donald Trump and his delegation during their brief stay in Manila. Describing the gesture as a 'taste of Manila', Marcos said he wanted the American president to sample one of the Philippines’ best-known fast-food brands.Marcos revealed the gesture on Wednesday during his meeting with Trump at the presidential palace, saying he had arranged the delivery the previous night because the US president was pressed for time.“Since you’re strapped for time, I thought a taste of Manila might be good. So last night, I asked my staff to have some Jollibee delivered as a late night snack for you and your delegation,” Marcos said.He described Jollibee as a popular Filipino chain and highlighted its fried chicken as one of its main offerings. Marcos also made a claim about the brand’s popularity in the US, drawing an approving response from Trump.“Jollibee … is a very, very popular chain. And one of their main products is fried chicken. And we are very proud to say that we have surpassed KFC in the United States in terms of popularity,” Marcos said according to news agency AP.“Oh wow. Fantastic,” Trump replied.“So we thought that that will give you a taste of, of, of Manila,” Marcos continued.“And, I think, I hope some of your staff was also able to partake.”“You have been working very hard, Mr. President, so just think of it as providing extra energy for all the work that you have to do that you have done and continue to do, and that is in front of you,” he added.It was not clear whether Trump had actually eaten the food.The gesture also appeared to draw on Trump’s known preference for fast food, particularly McDonald’s.In April, Trump received two bags of McDonald’s delivered to the Oval Office through DoorDash, in an event organised by the White House to promote an administration initiative on taxes on overtime and tips.“I like cleanliness, and I think you’re better off going there than maybe someplace that you have no idea where the food’s coming from. It’s a certain standard,” Trump said in a 2016 interview with CNN.Jollibee, which began as an ice cream business in Manila in the 1970s, has grown into one of the Philippines’ best-known brands. The company operates more than 1,600 outlets across 17 countries, with an expanding presence in the US.
Article Summary: Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arranged a late-night delivery of fried chicken from homegrown fast-food chain Jollibee for US president Donald Trump and his delegation. Describing the gesture as a 'taste of Manila', Marcos said he wanted the American president to sample one of the Philippines' best- known brands.

Article Title: Girl travels alone from Jharkhand to Mumbai after befriending boy on Instagram; here's how GRP found her
Article Text:
(Representative image) A 17-year-old girl from Jharkhand ran away to meet a boy she befriended on Instagram.

MUMBAI: A 17-year-old girl from Jharkhand who ran away from home to meet a boy she had befriended on Instagram was rescued by the Government Railway Police (GRP) and child welfare groups at Dadar railway station. The girl had travelled to Mumbai on her own, hoping to meet the boy, who was expected to come from his hometown in Jalna. She has been placed in a children's home, police said.The Class XII student travelled to Dadar by a long-distance train on November 16. She then waited for the boy on a seat at the station. Later, she sent photographs of herself to her family, who immediately contacted the local police for help in tracing her.The Mumbai GRP received information about the girl from the Anti-Human Trafficking Squad. The Railway Protection Force (RPF) also received an alert through the Rail Madad portal.With the help of child welfare groups, including Child Helpline and Railway Children India, the GRP traced the girl to platforms 13 and 14 of Dadar station.After completing the necessary legal and administrative formalities at the Dadar GRP chowky, the girl was taken to JJ Hospital for a preliminary health check-up. She was subsequently admitted to a children's home in accordance with the procedures of the Child Welfare Committee to ensure her safety, accommodation, care and protection.Her family has been informed that she is safe and is on its way to Mumbai.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl from Jharkhand ran away from home to meet a boy she had befriended on Instagram. The girl had travelled to Mumbai on her own, hoping to meet the boy, who was expected to come from his hometown in Jalna. She has been placed in a children's home, police said.

Article Title: Viral stunt video lands five bikers in police net in Mumbai; watch
Article Text:
Five motorcyclists were arrested by police after a viral video showed them performing reckless stunt





MUMBAI: Mumbai police arrested five motorcyclists after a video of them performing dangerous stunts and riding recklessly on the Western Express Highway surfaced on social media.The video showed the riders engaging in risky manoeuvres on the busy road, putting the safety of other commuters at risk. Following the incident, the Andheri and Vile Parle police registered cases under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act, an official said.Andheri police launched an investigation and traced the five riders.The five motorcyclists identified as Sahil Mohammad Siraj (29), Javed Rafiq Maldar (25), Faizan Ahmed Khan (22), Kushal Dattaram Bhise (22) and Mohsin Mubarak Shaikh (19).Police also impounded the five motorcycles used in the incident. Further investigation is underway, the official said.
Article Summary: Mumbai police arrested five motorcyclists after a video of them performing dangerous stunts surfaced on social media. The video showed the riders engaging in risky manoeuvres on the busy road, putting the safety of other commuters at risk. Police registered cases under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Motor Vehicles Act.

Article Title: Nanded farmer found dead on rail tracks; 4 finance firm staffers booked for abetment
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Railway police have booked four employees of a finance company for abetment to suicide after the family of a 57-year-old farmer alleged that relentless loan recovery pressure and threats drove him to end his life.Datta Mohanrao Umate, a marginal farmer from Ganpur village in Nanded ’s Umri taluka, was found dead on railway tracks in the Bolsa area on Nov 15, a day after he left home and failed to return.Based on a complaint filed by his wife, Parvatibai Umate, Govt Railway Police in Nanded registered a case against four finance company employees.“We have registered a case of abetment to suicide against four finance company employees. Further investigation is underway to establish the circumstances leading to Umate’s death and verify the allegations against the employees,” said inspector Prakash Waghmare.According to the family, Umate had borrowed Rs 1.5 lakh from the finance company’s Nanded branch in 2018 to build a house. While he had regularly repaid instalments, about Rs 1 lakh remained outstanding.Parvatibai and her son, Shankar, alleged that recovery agents repeatedly visited their house, demanded immediate repayment and threatened to seal the property if the dues were not cleared.Matters escalated on Oct 17 when a confrontation allegedly broke out between the recovery agents and Umate’s family. The finance company employees subsequently lodged a complaint at Umri police station, following which a case was registered against Umate and his family members.The family alleged that the visits and pressure continued even after the police complaint, pushing the farmer into severe mental distress. Umate left home on Nov 14 and went missing. His body was found on railway tracks the next morning. Railway police recovered the body and launched an investigation.The case has renewed scrutiny of loan recovery practices in the state. It comes weeks after another controversy involving farmer Chandrakant Shinde, who was allegedly assaulted and detained by finance company employees over loan recovery before being found dead under suspicious circumstances. The incident had triggered public outrage and police action.
Article Summary: Datta Mohanrao Umate, a marginal farmer from Ganpur village in Nanded ’s Umri taluka, was found dead on railway tracks on Nov 15. His family alleged that relentless loan recovery pressure and threats drove him to end his life. The case has renewed scrutiny of loan recovery practices in the state.

City police’s anti-narcotics cell seized drugs worth roughly Rs 1.3 lakh and arrested a 53-year-old man allegedly selling drugs from his scooter near a temple in the Buddhi Lane area on Tuesday.The accused, Anil Suryawanshi, was caught during a trap laid by the anti-narcotics cell after a tip-off about drug peddling near Lodhyashwar Mahadev temple.Police recovered 31.6 grams of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs 94,950, 90 Nitrazepam tablets valued at Rs 36,000, a mobile phone and a Honda scooter. Police are now probing the source of the narcotics and whether he was linked to a wider drug distribution network.“Acting on specific intelligence, our anti-narcotics team conducted a planned operation and seized the drugs before they could be sold to consumers. We appeal to people to share credible information about drug trafficking and substance abuse. Article Title: ​District admin orders action against colleges charging exam fees despite waiver
Article Text:
The fee waiver itself has benefited 2,96,114 BAMU students appearing for undergraduate and postgraduate examinations

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district administration has ordered action against colleges and principals allegedly collecting examination fees from students despite a fee waiver announced by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (Bamu).In a recent letter to BAMU, resident deputy collector Janardhan Vidhate directed the university to take immediate action against such colleges in accordance with state govt rules.The order came after Rahul Makasare, leader of the Vanchit Bahujan Yuva Aghadi, submitted a representation alleging that several colleges and principals were still collecting exam fees from students.“Colleges that collected exam fees should be ordered to immediately refund the amount. Also, exam fees paid by the wards of distressed farmers should be refunded on a priority basis,” he said.Bamu administration said students who had already paid examination fees despite the state govt’s drought-related waiver will now get their money back from their colleges, with the varsity having already handed over the refund cheques.“We directed 34 colleges to immediately refund students after they took back cheques totalling Rs 1,36,44,756 on Nov 6 and 7,” Bamu’s examinations and evaluation board director B N Dole said.“The university kept its examination department open during the Diwali holidays to facilitate the process. Overall, 51 colleges had collected fees from 25,074 students,” he added.The fee waiver has benefited 2,96,114 Bamu students appearing for undergraduate and postgraduate examinations in the winter session. With around 3,000 first and second-year students of the main campus and the Dharashiv sub-campus, the total benefit will reach nearly 3 lakh students.Faculty-wise, 61,771 students are from commerce and management, 89,790 from humanities, 10,819 from interdisciplinary studies, and 1,33,734 from science and technology, Bamu authorities said.
Article Summary: The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district administration has ordered action against colleges and principals allegedly collecting examination fees from students. The order came after Rahul Makasare, leader of the Vanchit Bahujan Yuva Aghadi, submitted a representation alleging that several colleges were still collecting fees. The fee waiver has benefited 2,96,114 Bamu students appearing for undergraduate and postgraduate examinations in the winter session.

Article Title: Beed collector cancels arms licence of Walmik Karad’s son over multiple criminal cases & video showing him carrying firearm tucked into his waist
Article Text:
Beed collector Vivek Johnson

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

Beed Collector Vivek Johnson has cancelled the arms licence of Sushil Karad, son of former Parli municipal council president Walmik Karad, citing multiple criminal cases against him and a viral video that allegedly showed him carrying a firearm tucked into his waist.The decision comes as scrutiny intensifies on associates of Walmik Karad, the prime accused in the murder of Massajog sarpanch Santosh Deshmukh. Confirming the action, Beed superintendent of police Navneet Kanwat said, “Licensed firearms are issued and meant for the licence holder’s personal safety. The firearms are not meant for boasting or threatening people.” He said the district police had communicated the matter to the collector, leading to the licence cancellation on Nov 3.According to police, Sushil was issued the firearm licence in 2020. Johnson invoked Section 17 of the Arms Act, 1959, to revoke the licence, observing that the licence-holder’s conduct was irresponsible and posed a potential threat to public safety and law and order.The collector’s order referred to a zero FIR registered at Parli city police station in Oct against Sushil and others following a court order. The case included charges under IPC sections 307 (attempt to murder), 323 (voluntarily causing hurt), 324 (causing hurt with dangerous weapons or means), 330 (causing hurt to extort a confession or information), 342 (wrongful confinement), 354 (assault or criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage, or knowing it is likely to outrage, her modesty), 452 (house-trespass or house-breaking after preparation for causing hurt), 504 (intentional insult), 506 (criminal intimidation) and 509 (words, sounds, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman), besides provisions of the Arms Act, and Section 8 of the Pocso Act According to the allegations cited in the order, Sushil, along with other accused, assaulted the complainant’s husband, threatened to kill him while brandishing a weapon, and allegedly molested the complainant’s minor daughter.Johnson also took note of a video circulated on social media and other platforms that allegedly showed Sushil carrying a firearm in public. The order stated that such display violated the conditions of the arms licence and could create fear among citizens, disturb public peace and increase the possibility of misuse of the weapon.The order further noted that Sushil had faced allegations in other cases involving offences under the Pocso Act, assault on women, intimidation of family members, forcible property takeovers and unlawful possession of vehicles.The action comes in the backdrop of the investigation into the Dec 9, 2024, murder of Massajog sarpanch Santosh Deshmukh, in which Walmik is the prime accused. Deshmukh was allegedly abducted, taken to a farm and brutally assaulted before being murdered.
Article Summary: Beed Collector Vivek Johnson has cancelled the arms licence of Sushil Karad, son of former Parli municipal council president Walmik Karad. Johnson invoked Section 17 of the Arms Act, 1959, to revoke the licence, observing that the licence-holder’s conduct was irresponsible and posed a potential threat to public safety and law and order.
